query: North Korea nuclear test 2026 - any signs of imminent 7th nuclear test, activity at Punggye-ri test site, recent statements or preparations mid-2026
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings:

**As of mid-July 2026, there is no publicly reported evidence of an imminent 7th North Korean nuclear test.** Key points:

1. **Technical readiness is complete, decision is political** — South Korea's Defense Intelligence Agency (Nov 5, 2025) assessed North Korea can test "on short notice" at Punggye-ri Tunnel No. 3; "the only remaining trigger is Kim Jong Un's political go-ahead." Preparations there have been assessed as essentially finished since 2022 ("Waiting for Kim").

2. **Tactical restraint amid diplomacy** — Analysts assessed NK would deliberately *suppress* a 7th test in 2026 to avoid derailing a potential Trump-Kim summit. Trump signaled renewed interest at the G7 (June 19, 2026), and think tanks flagged rising summit prospects.

3. **Arsenal expansion via non-testing means** — In early June 2026, Kim inspected a new fissile-material production plant, claimed weapons-grade output "more than doubled" in 5 years, and vowed "exponential" nuclear expansion — but announced no test. NK continued missile (not nuclear) tests through 2026.

4. **Caveat on data vintage** — The most authoritative public satellite-imagery analyses (CSIS/Beyond Parallel) are dated 2024 and earlier; the key recent readiness signal is the November 2025 ROK intelligence assessment. No July 2026-specific satellite report confirming new imminent-test indicators was located.

The full report and structured data (10 sources, 4 data points, 10 key facts) have been submitted via the StructuredOutput tool.

key_facts: No 7th North Korean nuclear test has occurred or been reported as imminent as of mid-July 2026; the last (6th) test was September 2017.

South Korea's Defense Intelligence Agency (Nov 5, 2025 National Assembly briefing) assessed NK can conduct a 7th test 'on short notice' with activity focused on Tunnel No. 3; the only remaining trigger is Kim Jong Un's political decision.
Technical preparations at Punggye-ri Tunnel No. 3 have been assessed as essentially complete since 2022 (US-ROK consensus), described as 'Waiting for Kim'.
Analysts (The Diplomat, Dec 2025) assessed NK would deliberately suppress a 7th nuclear test in 2026 to avoid derailing a possible Trump-Kim summit.

On June 3-4, 2026, Kim Jong Un inspected a new nuclear-material (fissile) production factory and vowed an 'exponential' increase in nuclear forces, claiming weapons-grade material output more than doubled in five years — but announced no test.
In late June 2026, at the 9th Central Committee 2nd plenary meeting, Kim again called for substantial nuclear arsenal expansion.
On June 19, 2026, Trump hinted at a new approach to North Korea, telling ROK President Lee that 'the time had come to pay attention to the North Korea issue.'

North Korea continued ballistic and cruise missile tests through 2026 (e.g., April 2026 ballistic launches, Oct 2025 'Fire Arrow' cruise missile), but these are missile tests, not nuclear detonations.
Punggye-ri is North Korea's only known nuclear test site; the 2017 test yielded an estimated 100-250 kilotons.
No public satellite-imagery report specifically dated July 2026 confirming new imminent-test indicators was located; the key recent readiness signal is the Nov 2025 ROK DIA assessment.
